newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - August 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - August 4.

DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- RJB OFFERS TO CUT COAL PRICES

RJB Mining, the UK's biggest coal producer, has proposed to cut its prices by 11.5 per cent so electricity tariffs can be reduced by 7.5 per cent, as part of a package introduced as an attempt to maintain coal sales when the domestic energy market is opened to competition in 1998. The offer will also bring the prices of coal produced in Britain and the cheap coal available on the international market closer together.
-- CAPITAL & REGIONAL NETS 30M STG IN YEAR

Martin Barber's specialist retail and leisure group, Capital & Regional Properties, has reported record net proceeds totalling over 30m stg from the sale of investment trading and joint portfolio properties to date in 1997. The sales are in line with company estimates, and continue Capital & Regional's concentration on the core areas of retail and leisure property.
-- MCI DEAL 'TO DENT PROFITS AT TELECOM'

According to figures from Dresdner Kleinwort Benson, British Telecom would be more profitable if it remains independent than if it goes ahead with its merger with MCI. DKB reports if BT were to remain independent its pre-tax profits for 1997 would be 2.8bn stg, rising to 3bn stg next year and 3.4bn stg in 1999- 2000, while under the merged Concert label 1997 profits would be 2.99bn stg, 1998 profits would be 2.91bn stg and then 3.2bn stg in 2000.
THE TIMES
-- VIRGIN BANK TO TAKE ON THE CLEANERS

Richard Branson's Virgin Group have made proposals to set up a 24-hour banking operation, targeting well-paid professionals in their 30s and 40s who have become 'disillusioned with their own bank'. Virgin is looking to take on the traditional operators of current and deposit accounts such as First Direct, HSBC Holdings, NatWest, Barclays and Lloyds TSB.
-- SANATOGEN UP FOR BREAKFAST

Pharmaceutical group Roche, the manufacturers of Sanatogen multivitamins, are set to enter the breakfast market, with the launch of a fruit juice. The juice, Start Up!, contains almost twice as many vitamins as milk and is aimed at the 86 per cent of people who do not take vitamin pills. Roche marketing manager Sophia Smith predicts the drink could add 10m stg to Sanatogen's annual sales.
-- NEC'S NEW 65M STG WING TO CREATE 2,000 JOBS

NEC's National Exhibition Centre in Birmingham is to invest 65m stg on a new wing, an investment which should add 100m stg to the West Midlands economy per year and create 2,000 jobs. The company teamed up with Emap to fund the new wing, which will be the world's seventh largest exhibition hall. NEC plans to use the new wing to bid for the 2003 International Textile Machinery Exhibition.
THE GUARDIAN
-- FRAUD-BUSTERS SCOTCHED

A Guardian exclusive reveals fraud investigators could be faced with new barriers following devolution in Scotland, as the UK and Scottish jurisdictions drift further apart in their treatment of serious financial crime. Some are apprehensive devolution could lead to conflicting standards of regulation in Scotland compared with elsewhere in Britain, enticing fraudsters to move back and forth between borders.
-- REPORT TO WATER DOWN CADBURY RULES

The Hampel committee on corporate governance will unveil its interim report on corporate governance on Tuesday, a report expected to lead to much criticism from business groups. The committee is expected to propose a watering down of rules as proposed in the Cadbury and Greenbury committees, under the argument they force excessive regulation on directors.
-- SPECULATION FOCUSES ON 30BN STG SUPERBANK

A survey of the banking sector carried out by business accountants Dun & Bradstreet reveals a merger between NatWest and Barclays banks would result in a 30bn stg 'superbank', which would control 50 per cent of market share - the most potent combination of existing banks. NatWest is expected to come under pressure to explain its plans for its retail and investment bank arms and along with Barclays and HSBC will report profits this week.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- TELEWEST IN EARLY TALKS WITH NTL

US cable group NTL has begun formal talks with Telewest Communications of the UK concerning a possible merger, which could create a rival to Cable & Wireless Communications. Sources have also revealed United News & Media is interested in becoming involved in the deal, as it already has close ties with NTL, but the company has been unavailable for comment.
-- SPEND, SPEND, SPEND TO TRIGGER INCREASES

Calculations by David Walton of Goldman Sachs indicate the if the consumer spending spree continues, it will increase pressure on the Bank of England to raise interest rates into the second half of the year. Walton suggests as consumer windfalls stemming from free shares from building societies has injected up to 2bn stg into spending in the first half of 1997, with strong indications the trend will continue.
-- OUTGOING ITV NETWORK DIRECTOR IN JOB TALKS WITH GRANADA

According to Granada sources, ITV network director Marcus Plantin is in talks with the Group concerning the possibility of his joining the media and leisure conglomerate when he leaves his post at ITV in the autumn. Speculation in the TV industry points to Plantin taking over as Granada's head of entertainment, following the company's structural review, though the company denies any restructuring is in the plans for the near future.
